title: From the Synthi to the SYNTRX II
intro: The SYNTRX II is the second of Erica Synths’ instruments built on the idea of the EMS Synthi: no fixed signal path, every source and destination on a 16 × 16 matrix, a looping trapezoid envelope and a joystick. The first SYNTRX was a re-imagining of the Synthi AKS, approved by Peter Zinovieff, one of EMS’s founders; the SYNTRX II keeps the matrix under digital control and adds a high-pass and low-pass filter, an envelope follower, a delay and reverb, and a sequencer that plays on the matrix itself.

timeline.name: EMS VCS3
timeline.text: The original: three oscillators, noise, a ring modulator, a filter, a trapezoid envelope and a spring reverb, connected by pins in a 16 × 16 matrix, with a joystick. This app has the VCS3 too.

timeline.name: EMS Synthi AKS
timeline.text: The VCS3’s circuits in a briefcase, with a flat touch keyboard and a digital sequencer in the lid. It is the instrument the SYNTRX was modelled on.

timeline.name: Erica Synths SYNTRX
timeline.text: A re-imagining of the Synthi AKS, approved by Peter Zinovieff, of which 1056 were made: three oscillators, a resonant filter, a ring modulator, a spring reverb and a joystick, with the matrix an analogue mixer under digital control that stores its patches.

timeline.name: Erica Synths SYNTRX II
timeline.text: Two audio oscillators and a third that is mainly an LFO, a sample and hold, two external inputs with an envelope follower, a high-pass and low-pass filter in series, a ring modulator with an internal second input, the trapezoid with its own VCA, a delay or reverb developed with 112dB, a recordable joystick, 256 stored matrix patches and a 16-step piano-roll sequencer.

timeline.name: The March 2023 manual
timeline.text: The version this app follows. Its EFFECTS section has a DELAY / REVERB switch and its matrix an S&H Input column; earlier panels, as in some product photos, have a DELAY section and give that column to the delay time.

relatives.name: EMS VCS3
relatives.text: The SYNTRX II’s great-grandparent, also in this app: the same rows-and-columns idea with pins, a VCS3-style trapezoid and joystick, but no keyboard of its own, oscillators that need patching to follow one, and a spring reverb in place of the effects.

relatives.name: Erica Synths Bullfrog
relatives.text: Erica Synths’ educational synth, made with Richie Hawtin: a single-oscillator subtractive voice patched by cable or by plug-in voice cards, where the SYNTRX II patches on its matrix.

relatives.name: Erica Synths Steampipe
relatives.text: Another instrument developed with 112dB, who made the SYNTRX II’s delay and reverb: a physical-modelling synth of feedback loops instead of oscillators.
